title: Every build judged correct or not by code, a check that cannot be read never assumed passed
request: Know whether each model was built correctly by DCLab's rules.
plan: Eight checks from CLAUDE.md's rules and the gates.
Each fact from the build's own records or None with why.
correct only when every check passed.

decisions.decision: The verdict is code, not a model's opinion.
decisions.why: CLAUDE.md rule 5: deterministic code owns the judgement.

decisions.decision: export_reproduces stays unknown until the code export's check is in the records.
decisions.why: A check that cannot be read is never assumed passed.

findings.defect: A planted leaking feature must fail the build.
findings.scenario: A project kept final_fare as a feature with a leakage risk.
findings.fix: no_leaking_column fails and names the column.

findings.defect: The verdict read a stage status the studio never writes.
findings.scenario: A project that read its holdout twice was judged unknown on every check, not incorrect.
findings.cause: status == 'done' and 'started' were guessed; the engine writes 'completed' and 'started_at'.
findings.fix: Finished means completed or approved (graph.DONE); started_at read.

findings.defect: no_leaking_column passed on every real build.
findings.scenario: The engine never writes 'leak' into risk_features, so nothing could fail.
findings.cause: The fixture invented a leakage note the engine never writes.
findings.fix: Read the leakage stage's declared_leakage_features and heuristic_review_candidates against the data stage's column_roles; unknown without both records.

findings.defect: A missing contract was judged incorrect, and no build could be correct.
findings.scenario: A project without a prediction moment failed; export_reproduces was always unknown.
findings.cause: False for a missing fact; the export's check, recorded in project.exports.code, was never read.
findings.fix: None for a missing contract; export_reproduces from project.exports.code against the final run.

findings.defect: An absent holdout count passed holdout_read_once.
findings.scenario: int(None or 0) read as zero reads.
findings.cause: A default turned a missing fact into a pass.
findings.fix: None when no count is recorded.

findings.defect: beats_baselines compared the point estimate, guessed the metric's direction, and read an optional metric field.
findings.scenario: 0.51 [0.40, 0.62] passed against a 0.50 baseline; mase was judged higher-is-better.
findings.cause: Point estimate; a substring list; solution.metric is optional.
findings.fix: The interval's bound on the metric's side, the direction from solution_brief.HIGHER (unknown when absent), the final record's primary_metric.

findings.defect: On the real store, 693 of 715 builds were judged incorrect on uncertainty_said.
findings.cause: The engine writes the holdout interval as {low, high, method, draws}; the fixture (and the code) read a pair.
findings.fix: _interval reads the engine's dict (a bootstrap with 0 draws is no interval) or a pair; a record that says why it has none is unknown, not failed.
findings.test: tests/test_store_service.py (the fixture now writes the engine's dict)

outcome: Each build has a verdict with each check's status and why.
lessons: Unknown is a verdict of its own: it keeps a missing record from reading as a pass.
Write fixtures from the code that writes the records (a stage record copied from the engine), never from memory: invented shapes made every test pass while every real build was judged wrong.
Run a new builder on the real store before trusting its tests: the second fixture mistake was found only there.
